subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Retaliation and Its Consequences
description: Learn Retaliation and Its Consequences in one minute.

hook.text: A compliance officer reports accounting irregularities. She's moved to a windowless office. Her projects disappear.

buildup.text: Retaliation against whistleblowers takes many forms: termination, isolation, reassignment, and career sabotage.

discovery.text: Retaliation doesn't just hurt the individual. It sends a message to every other employee: stay silent or suffer.

twist.text: Companies that retaliate against whistleblowers face larger fines. Courts treat retaliation as evidence of guilt.

climax.text: Retaliation is the most effective way to destroy an ethics program. It proves the code of conduct is meaningless.

punchline.text: Punish the reporter. Silence everyone else. Guarantee more fraud.

quiz.question: How do courts view retaliation against whistleblowers?
options: As evidence of guilt that increases fines
As irrelevant to the original complaint
